tier_rationale: The scan tool only functions through BlueDriver's own app, and BlueDriver's own product page lists 'Create an account or log in with your existing credentials' as a required setup step before the app will scan a vehicle — an account mandatory at setup with no local-only path, which is a REJECT trigger regardless of whether the account is free. The rejection rests on that documented requirement alone. Whether the adapter also refuses third-party OBD apps was not established: the only indication found was an unanswered customer review on BlueDriver's own product page, and support declining to correct a reviewer is not evidence that the reviewer was right. It is recorded as an open question, not as a reason.
rejection_reason: Core function — reading and clearing codes — requires the BlueDriver app, and BlueDriver's own setup instructions make creating a BlueDriver account (or logging into an existing one) a required step before the app will scan a vehicle. An account mandatory at setup is a REJECT trigger in the decision table, and no documented local-only path around it exists. That single documented requirement is the whole basis for this verdict; the separate question of third-party app compatibility is treated as unresolved rather than as a second ground.
the_unplug_test: The adapter itself just relays OBD-II data over Bluetooth, but that is not the whole product: BlueDriver's own setup flow requires downloading the BlueDriver app and creating or logging into a BlueDriver account before you can scan a car, and the hardware is not built to pair with other apps. If BlueDriver's account service ever goes away, the reader is left holding a Bluetooth dongle with no supported app to talk to it.
offline_losses: Cannot begin a scan without first creating or logging into a BlueDriver account, per BlueDriver's own setup instructions.

sources.supports: Manufacturer's own product page setup instructions: 'Download the BlueDriver App from the App Store (iOS) or Google Play (Android)' then 'Create an account or log in with your existing credentials' — listed as required steps before scanning. Also emphasizes 'Zero Subscription Fees' (no recurring cost) but does not remove the account requirement. A customer review on the same page reports the device is 'Unable to support aftermarket apps like Dr Prius', with BlueDriver support directing the customer to email support rather than naming a compatible alternative.

BlueDriver's own support center lists 'How do I create a "BlueDriver Account"?' among its most-viewed articles, corroborating that account creation is a routine, expected part of using the product rather than an optional extra.

BlueDriver's own vehicle-compatibility page describes compatibility only in terms of vehicle year/make/model and BlueDriver's own product line (Pro, MAX); no third-party app or software is named anywhere on the page.

alternatives.why: Same OBD-II Bluetooth scan-tool job, but the adapter is openly documented as compatible with 17 named third-party apps (Torque, Car Scanner, OBD Fusion and others) and its own app describes no mandatory account step — D1 rather than REJECT.

open_questions: Whether the MX+-style third-party app compatibility exists here at all is unresolved. BlueDriver names no third-party-compatible app on its own site, but absence of a marketing claim is not a documented restriction, and the one customer report suggesting incompatibility is Class C at best. Settling this would strengthen the alternative recommendation, though it would not change the verdict.

Whether the BlueDriver account can be bypassed entirely (e.g. a guest mode) was not found in any manufacturer documentation reached in this run — only the setup instructions and support-article title were confirmed, not a live app install.

Whether BlueDriver's app functions fully with the phone's own network connection blocked once an account exists (i.e. whether the account gate is a one-time setup cost or a persistent per-session requirement) is unresolved.
No FCC search was performed for this device; not load-bearing for the REJECT verdict, which turns on the account requirement rather than the radio.
notes: Distinguish from OBDLink MX+ (obdlink-mx-plus, D1) in the same subcategory: same job, opposite design. BlueDriver is made by Repairify; Repairify/BlueDriver has no entry in data/vendors.json and no incident was found in this run — the REJECT here is about the as-sold account requirement, not a post-purchase change in behavior, so it is not a vendor_risk ledger case.

changelog.change: First published as REJECT: mandatory BlueDriver account at setup, closed to third-party apps.

local_replacement_note: No documented way to use this specific adapter with a non-BlueDriver app or without a BlueDriver account; a reader wanting a locally-usable OBD-II Bluetooth adapter should buy one built for third-party apps instead (see alternatives).
